newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: DB sees slight rise in operating contributions.
newsitem.headline: DB sees slight rise in operating contributions.

text.p: Brewer DB Group said on Wednesday it expected a slightly higher contribution from operations in the current year.
DB said this would stem from consistent brand portfolio management and clear operational focus.

DB earlier reported a net profit of NZ$30.37 million for the year to September 30, up from $17.34 million a year earlier. It said it proposed to cancel three out of every four shares and return 60 cents tax-free to shareholders for each share cancelled.
DB said cutting prices in the liquor industry produced only short-lived effects on market share and its aim was to be better, not cheaper.
DB said too many industry players in New Zealand had tended to take the short cut of cutting prices in order to grow or protect volume.

"In our competitive and contracting beer, wine and spirits markets, this can only lead to similar adjustments from other players. A possible effect on market share will therefore be short-lived and the final result is a loss of value throughout the business chain," it said.

"DB Group is firmly committed to the creation of value through the consistent building of consumer franchise for each of its brands in its area of strength and role within the respective portfolios. We believe that being 'better' and not necessarily being cheaper is the way to create sustainable returns for our shareholders."
DB is 59.8 percent owned by Asia Pacific Breweries Ltd, a venture between Heineken NV and Fraser and Neave Ltd . -- Wellington Newsroom 64 4 4734 746
